correctness.rationale: The claim applies to any finite T⊂Z with at least four distinct integer parameters, in the standard (t,t²,t³) monomial lattice Z³, span L=maxT−minT≥3. Integer translation is a triangular unimodular change of lattice coordinates. For four ordered vertices with positive integer gaps x,y,z, the Vandermonde tetrahedral volume is V=xyz(x+y)(y+z)(x+y+z)/6, and projected (t,t²) quadrilateral area is A=(x+y)(x+z)(y+z)/2. From Fu Liu’s established dimension-three integral cyclic-polytope Ehrhart coefficients E(m)=1+Lm+Am²+Vm³, reciprocity yields I=V−A+L−1. Direct independent SymPy reconstruction gives a 48-term nonnegative integer polynomial D=6[I−2*binom(L−1,3)] after x=u+1,y=v+1,z=w+1, with v-independent part uw(positive polynomial) and every coefficient of v¹,...,v⁴ strictly positive. Thus I≥2 binom(L−1,3) for all positive gaps and equality exactly y=1 and (x=1 or z=1). Taking any four vertices of arbitrary T containing both endpoints gives an inscribed tetrahedron, whose interior integer points are interior to C3(T), proving the all-cardinality lower bound; hollowness forces L=3 and four consecutive parameters. The checker’s exact barycentric enumeration for seven small tetrahedra supplements the global polynomial certificate, not substitutes for it. Equalities for >4 vertices are deliberately not classified.
